0.title: Releasing the libraries
0.content: How an agent publishes the HCERT libraries (STT-NFR-002) once the owner has supplied credentials. Nothing is published yet. No GitHub workflow publishes and no workflow holds a credential: CI runs only the dry runs below, in the check, kotlin and rust jobs of .github/workflows/requirements-kg.yml. An agent runs the commands here, from a clean checkout of the release tag, and stops at the first failure.

1.title: What is published
1.content: One version for all of them, from VERSION (STT-NFR-001), with an entry in CHANGELOG.md that cites each smart-trust changes.md entry it implements. | Registry | Coordinates | Built by | . | Maven Central | io.github.litlfred:hcert-api, io.github.litlfred:hcert-core (Kotlin Multiplatform: the root module, plus -jvm and -js) | gradle -p tools/hcert-kotlin publishDryRun | . | crates.io | litlfred-hcert (library name hcert) | cargo package in tools/hcert-rust | . | npm | @litlfred/hcert-kotlin-js (Kotlin/JS ES module) | tools/release-packaging/assemble-npm.mjs | . | npm | @litlfred/hcert-component (the Rust WebAssembly component, transpiled with jco) | tools/hcert-rust/build-component.sh, then assemble-npm.mjs | . The coordinates follow the repository’s GitHub org (the owner’s decision of 2026-10-23). Their single source is "repository": "<org>/<name>" in smart-trust-tools.json: the Maven group is io.github.<org> (a namespace the org can verify on the Sonatype Central Portal through GitHub), the npm scope is @<org>, and the crate is <org>-hcert, because crates.io has no namespaces (the Rust library itself stays hcert). The Gradle build and tools/release-packaging/coordinates.mjs derive them; check-version.mjs fails if Cargo.toml, a POM or a package.json disagrees. Moving the repository to another org (say, WorldHealthOrganization) means changing that one field, renaming the crate in Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock as the check asks, and verifying the new namespaces below. The Kotlin package root stays who.smart.trust. Android uses the -jvm jar as it is; there is no AAR until an androidTarget() exists.

2.title: Once, before the first release
2.content: . | Licence. Apache-2.0 (the owner’s decision of 2026-10-23; OI-14). LICENSE is the official text from apache.org (sha256 cfc7749b…3d30); the crate ships its copy tools/hcert-rust/LICENSE (the check requires it to be identical), assemble-npm.mjs copies it into each npm package, and every jar carries it as META-INF/LICENSE. | Maven Central. Sign in to https://central.sonatype.com with the litlfred GitHub account; the io.github.litlfred namespace is verified by that. Generate a user token (View Account → Generate User Token): it is a name and a password, CENTRAL_TOKEN_USER and CENTRAL_TOKEN_PASS below. | Signing key. Central requires an OpenPGP signature on every file. Generate a key for releases, then publish its public half: gpg --quick-gen-key "Carl Leitner (smart-trust-tools releases)" ed25519 sign 2y gpg --list-secret-keys --keyid-format long # note the key id, KEYID below gpg --keyserver keys.openpgp.org --send-keys KEYID gpg --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com --send-keys KEYID . The key stays on the owner’s machine (or a hardware token). No key, token or passphrase is ever committed or given to a workflow. | crates.io. Sign in with GitHub at https://crates.io, verify an e-mail address, and create an API token scoped to publish-new and publish-update for the crate litlfred-hcert (CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN). | npm. The packages are scoped to the npm user litlfred. Create a granular access token with read and write on @litlfred/* (NPM_TOKEN), with two-factor authentication on the account. | .

3.title: Pre-release checks
3.content: From the repository root, on main, with a clean tree: . git status --porcelain # must print nothing git log -1 --format=%H origin/main # must equal HEAD; CI green on it cat VERSION # the version to release, no pre-release suffix . | Set the version, if it changes, in the three places that hold it, then let Cargo update its own entry in the lock (no other crate moves): echo 0.1.0 > VERSION sed -i 's/^version = ".*"/version = "0.1.0"/' tools/hcert-rust/Cargo.toml # the [package] version, the only line it matches (cd tools/hcert-rust && cargo update --workspace --offline) . | In CHANGELOG.md, replace — unreleased in the version’s heading with the date (## [0.1.0] — 2026-11-02), make sure every wire-format or subclaim-default change cites its smart-trust changes.md entry, and point the link at the tag ([0.1.0]: https://github.com/litlfred/smart-trust-tools/releases/tag/v0.1.0). A wire-format or subclaim-default change needs a major or minor bump. | Run the checks CI runs, and the dry runs: node tools/release-packaging/check-version.mjs bun run check:req-nodes python3 tools/test-plan/make_test_plan.py --check python3 tools/wit2kotlin/wit2kotlin.py --check gradle -p tools/hcert-kotlin --no-daemon compileKotlinJvm compileKotlinJs :hcert-core:jvmTest :hcert-core:jvmTestCoverageCheck :hcert-core:compileProductionLibraryKotlinJs (cd tools/hcert-rust && cargo test --locked && cargo test --locked --features qr --test api) . | Commit (Release 0.1.0), push to main of litlfred/smart-trust-tools, wait for CI to pass on that commit, then tag it with a signed tag and push the tag: git tag -s v0.1.0 -m "smart-trust-tools 0.1.0" git push origin v0.1.0 . | . Every artefact is then built from a fresh clone of the tag, never from a working copy: . git clone --branch v0.1.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/litlfred/smart-trust-tools.git /tmp/stt-release cd /tmp/stt-release bun run cat mount:lock && bun install # the mounted layers, for check:req-nodes . toolchain/node_tools.sh # jco, from the lockfile, no install scripts .

4.title: Maven Central (Central Portal bundle upload)
4.content: . | Publish into the build-local repository and check the result. Every archive is reproducible (no timestamps, fixed order), so building the tag twice from a fresh clone gives the same jars, klibs, sources jars and POMs. The Kotlin Gradle plugin (2.0.21) writes the org.gradle.libraryelements attribute into hcert-api’s .module files or not depending on which tasks the build runs, so run exactly this command: gradle -p tools/hcert-kotlin --no-daemon publishDryRun node tools/release-packaging/check-version.mjs tools/hcert-kotlin/build/maven-dry-run . publishDryRun lists, for each of hcert-api, hcert-api-jvm, hcert-api-js, hcert-core, hcert-core-jvm and hcert-core-js: the .pom, the .module (Gradle metadata), the main artefact (.jar, or .klib for -js), -sources.jar, -javadoc.jar (the module README; the KDoc is in the sources) and, for the root modules, -kotlin-tooling-metadata.json. Gradle writes .md5, .sha1, .sha256 and .sha512 beside each. | Sign every artefact (not the checksums, not maven-metadata.xml): repo=tools/hcert-kotlin/build/maven-dry-run find "$repo" -name 'maven-metadata.xml*' -delete find "$repo" -type f ! -name '*.md5' ! -name '*.sha1' ! -name '*.sha256' ! -name '*.sha512' \ -exec gpg --local-user KEYID --armor --detach-sign {} \; find "$repo" -name '*.asc' -exec gpg --verify {} \; . | Bundle the repository layout and upload it, as a deployment the owner releases by hand (USER_MANAGED): (cd "$repo" && zip -qrX ../central-bundle-0.1.0.zip io) token=$(printf '%s:%s' "$CENTRAL_TOKEN_USER" "$CENTRAL_TOKEN_PASS" | base64 -w0) curl --fail --request POST \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $token" \ --form bundle=@tools/hcert-kotlin/build/central-bundle-0.1.0.zip \ "https://central.sonatype.com/api/v1/publisher/upload?name=smart-trust-hcert-0.1.0&publishingType=USER_MANAGED" # prints the deployment id curl --fail --request POST --header "Authorization: Bearer $token" \ "https://central.sonatype.com/api/v1/publisher/status?id=DEPLOYMENT_ID" . Wait for "deploymentState": "VALIDATED"; on FAILED, the response lists each problem. Then release it, which cannot be undone: . curl --fail --request POST --header "Authorization: Bearer $token" \ "https://central.sonatype.com/api/v1/publisher/deployment/DEPLOYMENT_ID" . (or Publish on the deployment at https://central.sonatype.com/publishing/deployments). | .

5.title: crates.io
5.content: cd tools/hcert-rust cargo package --locked --list # exactly: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, README.md, DEPENDENCIES.md, LICENSE, src/*.rs cargo package --locked # builds the .crate on its own, from target/package/litlfred-hcert-0.1.0 cargo publish --locked --dry-run CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN=... cargo publish --locked . The tests are not in the crate: they read the shared vectors at ../../vectors, so they run from the repository. The component feature reads the WIT contract at ../../api/wit and so builds only from the repository too; the component is published to npm instead. A crates.io version cannot be replaced, only yanked (cargo yank --version 0.1.0).

6.title: npm
6.content: tools/hcert-rust/build-component.sh /tmp/stt-component gradle -p tools/hcert-kotlin --no-daemon :hcert-core:compileProductionLibraryKotlinJs node tools/release-packaging/assemble-npm.mjs --out /tmp/stt-npm \ --component /tmp/stt-component \ --kotlin-js tools/hcert-kotlin/hcert-core/build/compileSync/js/main/productionLibrary/kotlin node tools/release-packaging/check-version.mjs /tmp/stt-npm node tools/conformance-ts/run.mjs rust /tmp/stt-npm/hcert-component # the shipped files pass the suite node tools/conformance-ts/run.mjs kotlin /tmp/stt-npm/hcert-kotlin-js for p in hcert-component hcert-kotlin-js; do (cd /tmp/stt-npm/$p && npm pack --ignore-scripts --pack-destination /tmp/stt-npm) done sha256sum /tmp/stt-npm/*.tgz # record in the release notes . Then publish the tarballs that were checked, not the directories (scoped packages are private unless --access public): . printf '//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=%s\n' "$NPM_TOKEN" > /tmp/stt-npmrc npm publish /tmp/stt-npm/litlfred-hcert-component-0.1.0.tgz --access public --ignore-scripts --userconfig /tmp/stt-npmrc --otp=CODE npm publish /tmp/stt-npm/litlfred-hcert-kotlin-js-0.1.0.tgz --access public --ignore-scripts --userconfig /tmp/stt-npmrc --otp=CODE rm /tmp/stt-npmrc . An npm version cannot be republished once used, even after npm unpublish.

7.title: After publishing
7.content: . | Check that each coordinate resolves to the release (the STT-NFR-002 success criterion): curl -sI https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/io/github/litlfred/hcert-core-jvm/0.1.0/hcert-core-jvm-0.1.0.pom | head -1 curl -s https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/litlfred-hcert/0.1.0 | head -c 200 npm view @litlfred/hcert-component@0.1.0 version npm view @litlfred/hcert-kotlin-js@0.1.0 version . Maven Central can take up to an hour to show a released deployment. | Create the GitHub release for the tag with the changelog entry and the sha256 of each artefact. | Open the next entry at the top of CHANGELOG.md (## [0.2.0] — unreleased) and set VERSION and Cargo.toml to it in the same commit, so check-version.mjs keeps passing. | .

41.title: Lanes — who acts
41.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | HCERT issuing system | hcert-issuing-system | The HCERT side of the VHL Sharer (smart-trust: Issuer): a clinic system or national portal that issues HCERT certificates, embedding the Kotlin or Rust library. | . | Signing key holder | hcert-key-holder | The HSM, KMS, Android Keystore or WebCrypto key of a Trust Network Participant that signs the bytes the issuing system prepares; the library never holds the private key. | .

42.title: Steps
42.content: Every one of the 11 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Select the payload type and subclaimTask_SelectPayload | HCERT issuing system | — | Choose the logical model and the hcert subclaim for the use case from the registry QR Code Generation 2 defines: a DVC (key -6) when the certificate must verify offline, a VHL (key 5) when the records are larger than a QR code holds. | . | Assemble and validate the payloadTask_AssemblePayload | HCERT issuing system | — | Build the payload and validate it against its logical model (DVCMin, or the VHL payload), keeping elements the library does not know. | . | Build the CWT claim setTask_BuildCwt | HCERT issuing system | — | Wrap the payload in a CWT claim set: iss, iat, exp inside the DSC’s validity, and the payload at hcert (-260) under its subclaim. | . | Serialise as deterministic CBORTask_EncodeCbor | HCERT issuing system | — | Serialise the claim set as RFC 8949 deterministic CBOR, so the same claims always give the same bytes. | . | Prepare the Sig_structureTask_Prepare | HCERT issuing system | — | Build the COSE Sig_structure from the protected header (alg, kid = SHA-256 of the DSC, first 8 bytes) and the payload, and hand its bytes out to be signed. | . | Sign the bytes with the DSC keyTask_Sign | Signing key holder | — | The key holder signs the Sig_structure bytes with the DSC private key (ES256, or PS256) and returns the raw signature. The key never leaves it. | . | Attach the signature as COSE_Sign1Task_Finish | HCERT issuing system | — | Attach the returned signature to make the COSE_Sign1, checking it is the length the algorithm gives (64 bytes for ES256, r||s). | . | Compress with ZLIBTask_Compress | HCERT issuing system | — | Compress the COSE_Sign1 with ZLIB/DEFLATE, after signing, never before. | . | Encode as Base45Task_Base45 | HCERT issuing system | — | Encode the compressed bytes as RFC 9285 Base45, the alphabet QR Alphanumeric mode stores compactly. | . | Prefix HC1:Task_Prefix | HCERT issuing system | — | Prefix the context identifier HC1: to make the QR-ready string. | . | Render the QR code (Alphanumeric, EC Q)Task_Render | HCERT issuing system | — | The application renders the HC1 string as a QR code in Alphanumeric mode, error correction Q, with its own QR encoder. | .

208.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . 223.title: Write one JSON-LD node per IG artefact, and check a built site’s nodes
223.content: write turns an artefact index into artifact/<Type>-<id>.jsonld under a docs root, with no .json twin: one folio-ig-artifact-jsonld/v1 node per artefact, in borrowed vocabularies only (the FHIR RDF class, dcterms, schema.org, PROV), naming the artefact’s canonical URL, its representations and, for a compiled copy, what built it. With --root-resources (the IG site’s default) the first representation is the reduced <Type>-<id>.json the site serves at its root (local), the second the full copy in the AST cache by raw URL (mirror), and each index entry names the root file (schema:contentUrl). check is the kind’s QA: over a BUILT site, every artefact has its node and no node is an orphan, each node is its own file’s, no .json twin is served beside it, and every local resource it names is on the site. It also writes and checks the index node, artifact/index.jsonld (folio-ig-artifact-index-jsonld/v1): every artefact once, each entry naming its node. These are the assets the thin pages render. |   |   | . | Tool | ig-artifact-jsonld | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/tools/ig-artifact-jsonld.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/fhir-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | fhir-harness | . | source | fhir-harness/tools/ig-artifact-jsonld/ig-artifact-jsonld.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

263.title: Build an IG repository’s own site from its cached AST, with no instance declaration
263.content: The three checkout scripts the platform’s site build runs for a repository that holds an IG and only mounts layers (index.config.json): ig-site:ast restores the AST from the IG’s cache branch (ig-cache.sh restore) and judges it, refusing a stale, cannot-tell or absent one (a stale one is accepted for a preview by default, refused with SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=0, and never accepted for the root); ig-site:compose derives the artefact index from the AST (binding any IG API sidecars a layer above left in $SITE_WORK/ig-api/), writes the thin artefact pages, stages the IG’s input/ and sushi-config.yaml (menu read at build time, palette from the webpage theme of the top layer the repository mounts, edit links from its origin) and composes it at the ROOT of the host site source; ig-site:publisher-pages serves each of the AST’s resources once, as <Type>-<id>.json at the root (no ast-data/ mirror) — reduced (minified, no narrative, no ELM data, the ELM attachment pointing at the full copy) when the pages read the full resources by raw URL from the AST cache commit, and off with SITE_ROOT_RESOURCES=0 — the artefact index (or fhir-artifact-index/index.ref.json, pointing at the cache’s copy) and the sidecars (or none, read from the cache), refuses a page wearing the IG Publisher’s chrome, repairs repeated element ids and stamps folio-build.json. Never runs the Publisher and never reads its output. Compose lists the pages it puts in the site in FOLIO_SITE_UPSTREAM_PAGES, so the site build reports the IG’s own dead links rather than refusing the publish over them. |   |   | . | Tool | ig-repo-site | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/tools/ig-repo-site.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/fhir-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | fhir-harness | . | source | fhir-harness/tools/ig-repo-site/ig-repo-site.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

264.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. 307.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. 330.title: Build each IG instance’s artefact index from the IG’s cached AST
330.content: Write each IG instance’s fhir-artifact-index/ at publish, so no IG instance commits one. 331.title: Skills it satisfies
331.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. Source: fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-build-pipeline.md. 346.title: Stage one IG as its own just-the-docs Jekyll site

378.title: Write an IG site’s static terminology index from the IG’s own cache
378.content: Read the IG Publisher’s expansions.json and txcache/, as ig-cache.sh restore leaves them, and write index.json (gzipped as index.json.gz over 1 MB): every code with its system and display, and each value set’s codes. 379.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. 410.title: Scan every page of a built IG site in a headless browser for markup shown as text
410.content: The checkout script ig-site:page-render-qa, the IG site build’s last final step: it serves the built site locally, opens the root pages and the artefact pages (not the JSON views, mappings views or redirect stubs) in headless Chromium, waits for each to draw, and lists every text block that shows markdown as text (bold, list markers, links, images, code, headings, tables, HTML tags), code and preformatted text left out. It writes assets/fhir-qa/page-render.json and the script the QA report’s “Page scan” panel draws it with. It reports and never fails the build: without a browser it writes why. |   |   | . | Tool | ig-page-render-qa | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/tools/ig-page-render-qa.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/fhir-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | fhir-harness | . | source | fhir-harness/tools/ig-page-render-qa/ig-page-render-qa.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

435.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. 450.title: Cut an IG release as a GitHub draft that carries its packages and AST, and report a version left untagged or unreleased
450.content: Gather a release’s files from a full Publisher build (package.tgz and its R4/R4B variants, and ast-data.zip, the IG’s AST with the Libraries’ ELM), say from sushi-config.yaml whether it is a pre-release, and make or refresh the GitHub DRAFT release for the tag with the files uploaded. The owner publishes the draft; a published release is never changed. check is the catch-up the AST refresh of the default branch runs (advisory): it reports a current version with no v<version> tag, naming the commit that set it for the owner to tag, and a tag with no release, for the owner to run ig-release.yml by hand. 475.title: Skills it satisfies
475.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. ig-build-pipeline . The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. 485.title: Tools — fhir-harness
485.content: The Tool nodes fhir-harness declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 37Tool nodes 9skills satisfied 37invoked as a shell command 0reachable over MCP

486.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to full commit SHAs
486.content: Rewrite every third-party uses: owner/repo@ref outside the declared staging-only workflows to @<full commit SHA> # <ref>, so Dependabot keeps the pair current. A tag resolves to its PEELED commit (an annotated tag’s object is never pinned), else a branch head, by git ls-remote with argv. A ref that resolves to nothing, or to more than one commit, is refused and reported, never guessed. This repository’s own reusable workflows are first-party and left alone. 566.title: Where to drop a file — the queue’s upload URL
566.content: Compose the forge URL a person can drop a file at, from the layer’s own declaration: the uploads graph’s directory, resolved against the ROOT its scope names, expressed relative to the repository, and appended to the origin remote as GitHub’s /upload/<branch>/<path>. Every failure is NAMED and no URL is guessed — no declaration, no declared uploads graph, a declared queue absent from disk, no origin remote, and a non-github.com remote each return a reason and a remedy instead. 593.title: Skills it satisfies
593.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. repo-conversion . Lay folio-assistant over a repository that already exists, without losing or silently moving what is in it. Scans the tree read-only, classifies candidate files into library (external source) and content (authored here) with an explicit third bucket for what it cannot classify, scans outside the content tree for mathematical evidence and refutations, lists the content markers (an IG, a DAK, processes, work items, library, Lean, folio manifests) the harness could declare and declares only the ones the person picks, puts the three questions the scan cannot answer to the author as selections, and hands ingestion to one agent or a small swarm. Use when a user wants an existing repo converted to a folio, asks to import what is already there, asks whether their PDFs/notes/drafts can come along, or asks what else in a repository an existing harness could declare. Source: cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/repo-conversion.md. Also satisfied by: instantiate-harness. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/repo-conversion/{input,output}.schema.json). getting-started . Triage what a person means when they ask to create a folio, and route them. Five requests share one sentence — a folio in a new repo, folio-assistant overlaid on an existing repo, a second folio in a layer that already has one, a content object they called a folio, or something the filesystem cannot tell apart. Reads the repository facts, runs them through the folio-intent decision table, asks a selectable question for what facts cannot settle, scaffolds, and reports the published URL. Use whenever a user asks to create, start, set up, or initialise a folio, a paper, a DAK, an IG, or “folio-assistant” itself. Source: cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/getting-started.md. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/folio-init.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/folio-init/{input,output}.schema.json).

738.title: Is this repository’s cutover from the monorepo complete? Measured, condition by condition
738.content: Run in a separated repository. Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate: mounts (every declared layer on disk at its pin — remote-mount --check), declarations (every path a declaration names resolves — declaration-resolution), monorepo-paths (no wiring still names the monorepo: livesAt on it, a submodule of it, a reusable workflow called from it, a path into its old checkout — the one condition implemented here), import-direction and reference-direction (no layer reaches a layer above it), and site (the site builds from the mounts alone, every link resolving — build-instance-site --no-mount, only with --site). Findings inside a MOUNTED layer are listed and not counted: a defect in a layer pinned from upstream is fixed upstream and re-pinned. Exit 0 complete, 1 a condition failed, 2 a condition could not be determined or was not run — without --site the answer is never 0. |   |   | . | Tool | separation-cutover-check | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/separation-cutover-check.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/separation-cutover-check/separation-cutover-check.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

739.title: Skills it satisfies
739.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. The end-to-end method: the signals that trigger it, the preconditions, eleven stages each with the command that gates it, the owner’s decision points, how identifiers, QA and publication move, how the parent consumes the result, rollback, and the post-move sweep that a move between the pair owes before the parent re-pins. graph-detanglement owns stages 1–3; this skill owns the rest. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. 755.title: Mount remote harnesses at a pinned commit, only when trusted
755.content: Lay down each declared remote mount — a source.remote layer in the root index.config.json, or, in a folio with no index, a remoteMounts entry on its declaration (both at once is refused) — and its dependency closure, from another repository at a full commit SHA. Write the lock, index.lock.json (a legacy <name>.mount-lock.json is read, and renamed onto it when rewritten), and, with an index, regenerate the root .gitignore block that ignores each mount path. It READS the declared mounts and never writes them: a tool that changes a mount writes through writeDeclaredMounts into index.config.json. Before anything is checked out, each mount must pass the trust gate (schemas/kg/mount-trust.ts, rule H8): a person’s consent recorded for THIS pin, or a signature in a declared trust network. No signature verifier exists yet, so a signature alone is could-not-determine and does not mount. Unsigned and unconsented is refused. --staging mounts for a preview and needs neither. A directory id an override or mountDefaults names may be one the layer declares in its <name>.json or one it declares FROM WITHIN a declared directory (skills/skills.json naming voices), resolved at the pin through instanceDirectories; an id in neither is refused at plan time. tools on an override names Tools by id and mounts each one runnable: its definition (<tools dir>/<id>/<id>.ts), its implementation (the inProcess.module, or the script its bun run cat <key> resolves to) and their import closure, walked by bootstrap-tools’ importClosure (the one closure walker), as every declared directory that closure touches — the lock still records directories only. A hydrated mount lays each chosen directory down as its published index.hydrated.jsonld only: read from the pin’s git tree when a commit carries it, otherwise fetched from the pin’s subgraph index package (the subgraph-index-<sha> release asset subgraph-index-package publishes), its tarball checked against its folio-binary-release/v1 record, its manifest against the repository, pin and harness asked for, and each file against its sha256, SubgraphHydratedSchema and the subgraph IRI; the lock records the package’s URL and sha256 so a replay fetches the same bytes. --check compares the disk against the lock and never fetches. When a run CHANGES the lock, it then re-renders the agent surface (skill:commands → .claude/commands/, agent-memory → .claude/agent-memory/ and .agents/) from the checkout root, so a re-pin commit carries the skills and memory the new layers define; a generator that fails fails the run, and --no-agent-surface opts out. |   |   | . | Tool | remote-mount | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/remote-mount.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/remote-mount/remote-mount.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

831.title: Build, check and (on request) publish a layer’s own site, or a branches/ preview
831.content: From a checkout whose layers arrive by remote mount: mount the pinned closure, install, run the layer’s own gates (--pre), compose the harness chrome for THIS layer, run its source steps, build with Jekyll at the base path read from the git remote (/<repo>, or /<repo>/branches/<branch> for a preview), run the post-build steps (mount-instance-docs, pdf-viewer, set-html-lang, publish-id-lookup, rail-standalone-pages), and check that every relative or base-rooted link in every page resolves to a file under the site, reading each page with an HTML parser. Any failing step stops the run; a link that does not resolve means nothing is published. 856.title: Convert a checkout to a root index.config.json
856.content: Write the root index.config.json (folio-index-config/v1) that says which layers the checkout instantiates, where each comes from (source.local or source.remote) and which owns / (site.landing), from the root *.config.json files and the declaration’s remoteMounts. 914.title: Instantiate a harness over a repository that has none: pin, mount, open the setup-only PR, render the preview
914.content: The scripted step of the initiation process (getting-started.bpmn, the repo-conversion skill §4). Reads the harness’s declaration at its pin and every needs, transitively (a need beside the layer that needs it unless –repo-of says otherwise, at its default branch’s tip unless –pin says otherwise, its declaration’s name checked), seeds them all into the repository’s index.config.json with the consent given (remote-mount --seed --whole), sets site.landing to the harness, site.agentRun and mountApprovers, mounts the closure (remote-mount: index.lock.json and the .gitignore mounts block), installs it as root workspaces with the hoisted linker, writes the root bootstrap (.github/cat.ts and .github/mount-from-lock.sh from cat-harness-tools templates/root-bootstrap/) and sets the root’s cat script to bun .github/cat.ts, so bun run cat … mounts the layers itself on a later fresh clone, re-renders the agent surface from the mounted generators, runs the harness’s instantiate:<harness> checkout script when a mounted layer declares it, and commits on a branch (default harness/). Then, unless --local, pushes the branch, provisions gh-pages when absent (`pages-bootstrap --provision`), opens the setup-only PR, runs `prepare:` when declared (what the site is built from and nobody commits, such as an IG's AST) and renders the branch's preview at gh-pages branches// (`stage-local`); with --local the site is built and composed and nothing is pushed. It imports only node:*, so it runs from a fresh clone of cat-harness-tools before anything is mounted: it lays the platform's own closure, at the pins the repository will mount, into a temporary root to run the mount from. On a repository with nothing mounted yet, run the same file from a fresh clone: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools /tmp/cht && bun run /tmp/cht/scripts/instantiate-harness.ts …`. Two more flags, not declared as ports because no constrained type carries them yet: `--pin =` pins one layer of the closure, `--repo-of =<owner/repo>` says where a need lives. |   |   | . | Tool | instantiate-harness | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/instantiate-harness.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/instantiate-harness/instantiate-harness.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

915.title: Skills it satisfies
915.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. repo-conversion . Lay folio-assistant over a repository that already exists, without losing or silently moving what is in it. Scans the tree read-only, classifies candidate files into library (external source) and content (authored here) with an explicit third bucket for what it cannot classify, scans outside the content tree for mathematical evidence and refutations, lists the content markers (an IG, a DAK, processes, work items, library, Lean, folio manifests) the harness could declare and declares only the ones the person picks, puts the three questions the scan cannot answer to the author as selections, and hands ingestion to one agent or a small swarm. Use when a user wants an existing repo converted to a folio, asks to import what is already there, asks whether their PDFs/notes/drafts can come along, or asks what else in a repository an existing harness could declare. Source: cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/repo-conversion.md. Also satisfied by: folio-init. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/repo-conversion/{input,output}.schema.json). remote-mount . Bring a harness, and every layer it depends on, into a checkout that does not hold it, from another repository at a pinned commit, as declared directories with a lock: a source.remote entry in the downstream’s root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts on its declaration) and mountDefaults on the harness. Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/remote-mount.md. Also satisfied by: build-instance-site, index-config-migrate, kg-retrieve-npm, mount-from-lock, npm, subgraph-index-package. 931.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. archimate-models . ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model’s own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio’s staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source’s own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. 963.title: Skills it satisfies
963.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. The end-to-end method: the signals that trigger it, the preconditions, eleven stages each with the command that gates it, the owner’s decision points, how identifiers, QA and publication move, how the parent consumes the result, rollback, and the post-move sweep that a move between the pair owes before the parent re-pins. graph-detanglement owns stages 1–3; this skill owns the rest. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. Also satisfied by: mount-from-lock, package-exports, rewrite-moved-paths, separation-cutover-check. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/kg-separation/{input,output}.schema.json). kg-affordances . The four affordances of a conformant knowledge graph — browse, materialise, instantiate and copy-into-folio — which capabilities each requires, how each writing verb degrades cleanly when no write capability is available, and how copying an asset stamps KgAsset.source provenance. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/kg-affordances.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/kg-affordances/{input,output}.schema.json).

979.title: Rewrite paths that still name a moved file’s old layer — never in a record
979.content: After a move between two layers lands, find every mention <from>/<prefix>/<rest> in the scanned tree’s tracked files and rewrite it to <to>/<prefix>/<rest> only when the file exists under the destination root and not under the source root. 980.title: Skills it satisfies
980.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. The end-to-end method: the signals that trigger it, the preconditions, eleven stages each with the command that gates it, the owner’s decision points, how identifiers, QA and publication move, how the parent consumes the result, rollback, and the post-move sweep that a move between the pair owes before the parent re-pins. graph-detanglement owns stages 1–3; this skill owns the rest. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. Also satisfied by: declaration-resolution, mount-from-lock, package-exports, separation-cutover-check. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/kg-separation/{input,output}.schema.json).

990.title: Verify a separated repository from a fresh clone
990.content: Clone a separated sub-KG’s repository (with submodules, and any sibling checkouts it needs) into an empty scratch directory, install, and run its gates: its gates script, else its test script (a person may pass --gate on the command line instead; it is not part of this contract because it is a shell command). Reports green, red or unknown; an empty tree, a failed clone or a repository with no gate is unknown, never green. Catches what a rehearsal inside this checkout cannot, because a rehearsal shares this checkout’s node_modules and environment. 991.title: Skills it satisfies
991.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. sub-kg-lifecycle . A sub-KG is a knowledge graph staged as a directory inside a harnessed repository, declared as its own layer, that may later leave for a repository of its own. The lifecycle: declare it in place, grow it, stage it for separation (one import seam, the separation guard, a self-contained rehearsal), and then, each behind an explicit owner confirmation, create the repository, copy the staged contents in with history, re-point the declaration, verify on a fresh clone and delete the in-repo copy. The light sibling of kg-separation: use this for a DATA layer that leaves whole, and kg-separation when a graph must split into a content repository and a tools repository. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/sub-kg-lifecycle.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/sub-kg-lifecycle/{input,output}.schema.json).

1000.title: Skills it satisfies
1000.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. uml-overview . Read, regenerate or extend the UML class diagrams of a harness: one per harness and one per named sub-graph it declares, plus the harness object model. Every box is generated from a declaration and a schema, never drawn by hand, so a wrong diagram is fixed at the declaration or the schema, and a dashed “could not determine” box is a finding about the registry. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/uml-overview.md. Also satisfied by: uml-object-model. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/uml-overview/{input,output}.schema.json). kg-subgraph-layout . 1106.title: Check that an ArchiMate model’s fhir-actor tags point at the IG’s FHIR ActorDefinitions
1106.content: Actors come first: the IG’s ActorDefinitions are written from the DAK’s personas, and an ArchiMate model only points at them. For one model a layer’s cat-archimate.config.json names, this reads every element carrying the Archi property fhir-actor, whose value is an ActorDefinition’s canonical URL, and the IG’s ActorDefinitions: FSH InstanceOf: ActorDefinition under input/fsh/, and FHIR JSON under fsh-generated/resources/ or input/resources/, each canonical being <sushi-config canonical>/ActorDefinition/<id> unless its url says otherwise. It fails on a value that is not a canonical URL, a tag that names no ActorDefinition, an element kind that cannot be an actor (a data object, a goal), and a type mismatch (a #person actor on an application or technology element, a #system actor on a business actor or role). It warns about each ActorDefinition no element realizes; --strict makes that a failure. --json prints element → actors and actor → elements, for page back-links. It never writes an ActorDefinition or any FSH, and never matches boxes to actors by name. |   |   | . | Tool | archimate-actors | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/archimate-actors.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/archimate-actors/archimate-actors.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

1180.title: Screen a hand-over for injected instructions, field by field
1180.content: Before a model reads a sub-agent’s report, a delegated prompt, a tool result or a comment from someone who is not the principal, screen it against a declared schema whose top-level fields are control (steers what the receiver does) or data (content it reads). A finding in a control field, or any field the strict schema does not declare, is REFUSED, so a report cannot extend the delegator’s plan. A finding in a data field is QUARANTINED: the original is kept and marked, never stripped. The patterns are a deterministic tripwire (instruction overrides, role and turn spoofs, fence breaks, tool-call syntax, hidden Unicode, exfiltration links, pipe-to-shell), a mitigation and not a guarantee. 1204.title: Publish a folio’s or an IG’s site from the agent’s own checkout — the one agent publish path
1204.content: Build a repository’s site in the agent’s checkout and push it to the publish branch, as a preview or as the main site, without an Actions runner. Which build is read from the repository: a declared site.build recipe (built by build-instance-site), else the reusable workflow its own workflow files call — folio-staging.yml for a folio, the WHO SMART Base IG’s ghbuild.yml for a FHIR IG, whose build job is planned step by step and run as written. For an IG it then applies the harness chrome over the built output (sync-docs-harness, then rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site --instance <the IG>): every page gains the rail and the icon row #fa-navbar-row, and the IG’s own content is left byte for byte. A root publish is REFUSED when the chrome cannot be applied, and a clean root deploy is refused over any root whose index.html wears the icon row unless the new output does too, so a chromed root is never replaced by bare IG Publisher pages. Every run prints its plan first, and the plan lists the chrome step; --plan stops there, --dry-run composes the commit in a temporary worktree and pushes nothing, --artifact writes a claude.ai Artifact bundle instead. |   |   | . | Tool | stage-local | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/stage-local.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/stage-local/stage-local.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

1309.title: Replay a committed mount lock with nothing but Node
1309.content: Lay down every remote mount index.lock.json records — each layer fetched at the lock’s full SHA (sparse, blob-filtered), each directory verified against its treeDigest, a mismatch undone and reported — importing only node:*, so it runs on a fresh clone before any layer is present. It never decides what to mount: remote-mount writes the lock (and checks trust); this only replays it. Refuses to write over a path with tracked files or bytes that no longer hash to the lock. Exit 0 mounted/current, 1 missing, 2 could-not-determine. |   |   | . | Tool | mount-from-lock | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/mount-from-lock.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/mount-from-lock/mount-from-lock.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

1310.title: Skills it satisfies
1310.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. remote-mount . Bring a harness, and every layer it depends on, into a checkout that does not hold it, from another repository at a pinned commit, as declared directories with a lock: a source.remote entry in the downstream’s root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts on its declaration) and mountDefaults on the harness. Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/remote-mount.md. Also satisfied by: build-instance-site, index-config-migrate, instantiate-harness, kg-retrieve-npm, npm, subgraph-index-package. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/remote-mount/{input,output}.schema.json). kg-separation . Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. The end-to-end method: the signals that trigger it, the preconditions, eleven stages each with the command that gates it, the owner’s decision points, how identifiers, QA and publication move, how the parent consumes the result, rollback, and the post-move sweep that a move between the pair owes before the parent re-pins. graph-detanglement owns stages 1–3; this skill owns the rest. Bootstrap + bootstrap-tools and cat-harness + the tools layer are the worked examples. Source: cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/kg-separation.md. Also satisfied by: declaration-resolution, package-exports, rewrite-moved-paths, separation-cutover-check. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/kg-separation/{input,output}.schema.json).

1326.title: Publish a built site to gh-pages as a full replace
1326.content: Lay a built _site onto a gh-pages checkout as a FULL REPLACE and push it, keeping the open pull requests’ staging previews: each attempt re-reads the branch, re-runs restore-staging and keep-shared-payloads against what is on it now, replaces the tree, commits docs(gh-pages): site from <sha> and pushes. A rejected push is rebuilt, never rebased (a rebase would re-apply the replace over a preview a sibling just deployed), up to three attempts. A restore that cannot read the branch stops the publish. A site that matches the branch is a no-op, not a failure. It publishes and does not verify: the workflow’s verify step runs after it. |   |   | . | Tool | publish-gh-pages | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/publish-gh-pages.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/publish-gh-pages/publish-gh-pages.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

1406.title: Journeys viewer
1406.content: Draw every journey (user-scenario) and workshop (workshop) in the checkout as static pages at the route of the visualiser a layer declares for this Tool, <locale>/<instance>/<id>/: an index of all journeys, grouped by layer (each a sub-graph page), each parent’s parts nested under it in its order with optional and repeating parts marked (an older file’s partOf children after them, ordered along follows), and a plain DAK user scenario with no steps listed as one; one page per journey, its parts in order and the journeys it is a part of, a journey map with a lane and a feeling curve per persona, then each step, linked to the journey it includes, with its BPMN drawing (the step’s flow nodes highlighted), user stories, requirements, FHIR examples, building blocks, the DAK assets it uses (data sets, decision tables and indicators, linked into the IG) and ArchiMate views; and the workshop layer, the questions for the room on each step, a page per workshop and per module, job aids, and printable A3/A4 sheets; and each device screen (device-screen) that shows a step a workshop presents, drawn as a static device mock (phone, tablet, scanner, desktop, kiosk) with its owner beside it, in the workshop’s Device Demo, linked both ways with the walkthrough. A persona’s picture (meta.persona.avatar) is drawn wherever the persona appears. Layers below the declaring one are read through their declarations, so a downstream site shows the journeys of the layers it mounts too. |   |   | . | Tool | journeys-viewer | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/journeys-viewer.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/journeys-viewer/journeys-viewer.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

ALWAYS exits 0: the sweep runs it as if ! …; then, and a non-zero exit would print the report AND declare it unchecked every time CI is red. | boolean · A boolean switch — projects to a bare flag, with no value word | . | in | warn | Flag |   | Report only, never fail. No .. segments. | . | out | report | Markdown |   | One row per workflow. Five verdicts, not two: green, red, running, superseded (a red whose workflow file changed after the failing run, so the verdict is against code that no longer exists), and possibly-stale (a red that has not re-run in a week). Three exit codes carry them to a caller that reads no rows: 0 nothing is red, 1 something is, 2 COULD NOT LOOK — the API was unreachable, or --out could not be written. A caller must never read 2 as either verdict. --markdown and --warn always exit 0 by design, so a caller wanting the verdict uses neither. | string · Markdown text. For one model a layer’s cat-archimate.config.json names, this reads every element carrying the Archi property fhir-actor, whose value is an ActorDefinition’s canonical URL, and the IG’s ActorDefinitions: FSH InstanceOf: ActorDefinition under input/fsh/, and FHIR JSON under fsh-generated/resources/ or input/resources/, each canonical being <sushi-config canonical>/ActorDefinition/<id> unless its url says otherwise. 1668.title: Skills it satisfies
1668.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. process-state . Track where you are inside a running process — which task, in which swimlane, under which role — and recover deliberately when you find yourself outside it. Read before completing a workflow step, and whenever something unexpected interrupts one. 1701.title: Spreadsheet tabular metadata
1701.content: Read a workbook into a folio-tabular-csvw/v1 record, one CSVW table per rectangular block of cells. Blocks are split on empty rows, then on empty columns, so several tables on one sheet are found, each anchored at its real top-left cell (fac:anchor: sheet, A1 cell, row, column). Dates are read through the number formats in styles.xml, not misread as integer serials. A malformed part is refused rather than half-read. Reads the ZIP with node:zlib and SpreadsheetML with fast-xml-parser. 1741.content: For every figure a source publication declares, report whether the folio built from it has a block and how computable it is: missing, excluded (signed off), picture (a PNG crop), linked (a picture linked to a model view), computable (a diagram, a table or a figure rebuilt by ArchiMate, BPMN, DMN, Mermaid, a class diagram or a generator), or cited (a picture kept on purpose, signed off). 1742.title: Skills it satisfies
1742.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. figure-rebuild . Turn a figure into a computable diagram: every figure of a source publication when a folio is built from its L1 entry, and any hand-drawn figure in a folio, an IG or a demonstrator that is redrawn from a source. Every declared figure gets a block, and each one is rebuilt in the form its type calls for: an ArchiMate view, BPMN, DMN, a FHIR logical model, or an SVG generated from data, always from one schema-backed source. The PDF crop stays beside the rebuild as the cited source, and the rebuild keeps the original’s layout. The figure-coverage check counts what is missing and what is still only a picture. Source: folio-assistant-core/skills/library/ingestion/figure-rebuild.md. Also satisfied by: diig-phases-svg, smart-approach-svg. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/figure-rebuild/{input,output}.schema.json).

1768.title: Build the review sheet’s Apps Script and a document’s Config tab
1768.content: Builds Code.gs (--script), the one Google Apps Script every review sheet runs (from review-sheet.gs), and one document’s Config tab rows (--config), filled from the folio’s review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json, its review anchors and the draft’s pdf-line-map.json. The script keeps a public-comment review sheet’s links and joins current: each comment No. links to its comment page; Sections, Page and Line no(s) link to the page of the frozen review draft; Review Change Sets joins its comments, suggested revisions, feedback and dispositions, each No. n linking to its row; and on both tabs Agentic status lists each pull request of the change-set, linked, with its status and what it changed, from the Agent tab. It reads the document’s URLs, tab and column names and data from the sheet’s Config tab (visible, locked to the owner), which the agent writes from these rows. A person pastes the script (one file) into the sheet once (Extensions > Apps Script) and runs installTriggers; from then on the sheet rebuilds itself within about a minute of an edit, with no agent. With "mode": "drafting" in the config it builds the drafting sheet instead: one Contributor Feedback tab where each row is a change set (ids assigned by the script), Sections picked from the document’s table of contents and linked to it, and Issue and Agentic status from the Agent tab. |   |   | . | Tool | review-sheet-sync | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/review-sheet-sync.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

1800.content: A review-process task moves one review-comment/1.0.0 todo’s status (address, send back, resolve, adjudicate, withdraw) through transition(), which refuses any move the named BPMN task may not make. The comment is written to the folio’s todos graph (its declared todo-feedback directory) and, with --commit, committed to the edit-set’s FEATURE branch. 1865.title: Skills it satisfies
1865.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. dublin-core-renderings . Render a catalogue’s Dublin Core records in the two standard forms an outside reader can use: Dublin Core XML, which a harvester reads, and JSON-LD bound to DCMI Metadata Terms. Each rendering is published beside the item’s page. Covers which records get one, which XML form is used and why, how every field maps from the record’s own data (never composed), what cannot be expressed and how that is reported, and the gate. Read this before changing the mapping, adding a catalogue layer, or linking a rendering from a page. Source: folio-assistant-core/skills/library/catalogue/dublin-core-renderings.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/dublin-core-renderings/{input,output}.schema.json).

1881.title: Skills it satisfies
1881.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. review-comments . Reviewer comments on a folio’s edit-set, from a tagged pull-request comment to a structured todo on the review page. Covers the tag a reviewer types, how the comments are ingested into review-comment/1.0.0 todos, where the published review-comments.json comes from and when it refreshes, how a comment follows a renamed block and survives a removed one, who may change a comment’s status, and how to change this process. 1912.title: Check a review log and its repository’s issues for changes
1912.content: The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet’s Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository’s open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled no-sheet and, with --author, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check’s. Unchanged: it prints {"status":"unchanged"} and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell’s old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row’s Issue cell links yet (Title the issue’s title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): first paragraph, Issue the issue’s URL; a closed issue’s row marked closed), and closedRows, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log’s Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled change-set unless --label says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an issue-unlinked change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With --accept it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against. |   |   | . | Tool | review-log-watch | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch/review-log-watch.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

1931.title: Tools — folio-assistant-core
1931.content: The Tool nodes folio-assistant-core declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. 1940.title: HCERT library (Rust, native and WebAssembly)
1940.content: The Rust implementation of the HCERT pipeline: Base45, ZLIB, deterministic CBOR, COSE_Sign1 ES256/PS256 (RustCrypto p256, rsa, sha2), CWT, the DVCMin payload, the trust store (PEM, DER, GDHCN DID trustlist v2, trust domains), the section 11 verifier, two-phase issuance and Verifiable Health Links (payload, vhlink:/, the ITI-YY5 manifest, JWE dir/A256GCM with aes-gcm, the RFC 9421 signature base). It builds natively; as the WebAssembly component of the hcert world in api/wit (feature component, wit-bindgen; build-component.sh componentises and transpiles it with the pinned jco into an ES module for browsers and Node, whose only import, wasi:random, maps to crypto.getRandomValues); and as an import-free module with a JSON call surface for the live demos (js/hcert.mjs, with a TEST ONLY builder of self-signed DSCs). Every crate is pinned in Cargo.lock (DEPENDENCIES.md). |   |   | . | Tool | hcert-rust | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/smart-trust-tools/tools/hcert-rust.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/smart-trust-tools/smart-trust-tools.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | smart-trust-tools | . | source | tools/hcert-rust/hcert-rust.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

2048.title: Skills it satisfies
2048.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. hcert-select-payload . Step 1: choose the logical model and hcert subclaim for a use case, from the registry the IG defines. Source: skills/hcert/hcert-select-payload.md. Also satisfied by: hcert-rust. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/hcert-select-payload/{input,output}.schema.json). hcert-assemble-payload . Step 2: build and validate the payload against its logical model (DVCMin, or a VHL payload), keeping unknown elements. Source: skills/hcert/hcert-assemble-payload.md. Also satisfied by: hcert-rust. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/hcert-assemble-payload/{input,output}.schema.json). hcert-build-cwt . Step 3: wrap the payload in a CWT claim set (iss, iat, exp, hcert -260) inside the DSC’s validity. Source: skills/hcert/hcert-build-cwt.md. Also satisfied by: hcert-rust. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/hcert-build-cwt/{input,output}.schema.json). hcert-encode-cbor . Step 4: serialise as RFC 8949 deterministic CBOR, and decode untrusted CBOR within limits. Source: skills/hcert/hcert-encode-cbor.md. Also satisfied by: hcert-rust. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/hcert-encode-cbor/{input,output}.schema.json). hcert-sign-cose . Step 5: sign as COSE_Sign1 (ES256 or PS256) in two phases, the private key staying with its holder. Source: skills/hcert/hcert-sign-cose.md. Also satisfied by: hcert-rust. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/hcert-sign-cose/{input,output}.schema.json). hcert-compress . Step 6: ZLIB/DEFLATE after signing, and bounded inflation. Source: skills/hcert/hcert-compress.md. Also satisfied by: hcert-rust. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/hcert-compress/{input,output}.schema.json). hcert-encode-base45 . Step 7: RFC 9285 Base45, decoded strictly. Source: skills/hcert/hcert-encode-base45.md. Also satisfied by: hcert-rust. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/hcert-encode-base45/{input,output}.schema.json). hcert-prefix-context . Steps 8 and 9: the HC1: context identifier, giving a QR-ready string the application renders with its own QR encoder. Source: skills/hcert/hcert-prefix-context.md. Also satisfied by: hcert-rust. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/hcert-prefix-context/{input,output}.schema.json). hcert-verify . Verify an HC1 string or raw COSE: the steps upwards, trust lookup by kid, signature, key usage, time and payload; or read it explicitly unverified for triage. Source: skills/hcert/hcert-verify.md. Also satisfied by: hcert-rust. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/hcert-verify/{input,output}.schema.json). hcert-trust-list . Hold the trusted DSCs the host obtained (PEM, DER, GDHCN DID trustlist v2) and find every candidate for a kid. Source: skills/hcert/hcert-trust-list.md. Also satisfied by: hcert-rust. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/hcert-trust-list/{input,output}.schema.json). vhl-share . Issue a VHL: a key, documents encrypted as JWE dir / A256GCM, and the payload as a CBOR map at HCERT key 5 (journey J4.0). A plain SMART Health Link is issued by the same steps with its own carrier. Source: skills/vhl/vhl-share.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/vhl-share/{input,output}.schema.json). vhl-receive . Use a VHL: verify it, build the ITI-YY5 manifest request with its HTTP Message Signature, read the manifest Bundle and decrypt each document (journey J4.1). A plain SMART Health Link is received by the same steps, without the HCERT verification. Source: skills/vhl/vhl-receive.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/vhl-receive/{input,output}.schema.json). hcert-library-architecture . 2082.title: Tools — smart-trust-tools
2082.content: The Tool nodes smart-trust-tools declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 18Tool nodes 16skills satisfied 18invoked as a shell command 0reachable over MCP

2087.title: Tools
2087.content: As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 229Tool nodes 102skills satisfied 207invoked as a shell command 23reachable over MCP

2159.title: User journey coverage (DRAFT journeys J1 to J4)
2159.content: What the HCERT library must do for each step of the workshop storyline, and whether it does. OHS Player, OHS Stack and the CHW and wallet apps are consumers of the Kotlin library; rendering, scanning, storage, HTTP and FHIR record keeping are theirs. Source: stakeholder directive dir-journeys, 2026-10-20. | Journey step | Library capability | Status | . | J1 Country A clinic issues a DVC for each newborn vaccine (Hep B, polio) | DVCMin payload, one event per certificate (STT-PAY-003); no identity document for a newborn (STT-PAY-005); guardian name gn; any national vaccine code in vp (extensible binding) | Done: HcertIssuer.prepare / finish | . | J1 signs with the clinic’s DSC key held in Android Keystore or an HSM | Two-phase signing, no private key in process (STT-ISS-004, STT-COS-006) | Done | . | J1 printed paper QR, or SMS/MMS | HC1 string is QR Alphanumeric only (STT-QR-001); the app renders it at error correction Q | Done (rendering is the app’s) | . | J1 DEV keys and DEV trust list | Trust store loads GDHCN DID trustlist v2 documents (DEV, UAT, PROD alike) and PEM | Done: addDidDocument, addPem; the app fetches from the trust list distribution endpoints | . | J2 CHW, offline, reads the foreign QR to register the child and refer | Explicitly named unverified read, its result typed as unverified (STT-VER-011) | Done: HcertVerifier.readUnverified | . | J2 alternative: verify offline on the CHW device | Verification is synchronous and offline against a store the app filled earlier (STT-GEN-012, STT-VER-009) | Done; which one J2 uses is the journey’s open question | . | J3 Clinic verifies the foreign DVC | GDHCN verification in the STT-VER-001 order, typed failures (STT-VER-008), EKU check (STT-VER-004) | Done: HcertVerifier.verify, PR 129 vector verifies on JVM and Node | . | J3 imports the immunization into the domestic record | The verified DVCMin fields; mapping to FHIR R4 Immunization/Patient | Not in this library (the app maps). Worked examples in smart-trust-demo: TrustDemoJ3HepB and TrustDemoJ3Bcg, with their verification provenance | . | J3 adds the national schedule code beside the foreign vaccine code | The library passes the issuer’s vp code through unchanged and rejects nothing for an unknown code. The translation is a FHIR ConceptMap ($translate) the clinic EHR applies, adding the national coding and never replacing the issuer’s | Not in this library. Worked example in smart-trust-demo: ConceptMap TrustDemoProductToOnesaEpi (product → national schedule dose of Onesa, the demo’s fictional home country); a product with no entry goes to the nurse, whose decision is recorded (TrustDemoJ3Adjudication) and added to the map | . | J4.0 National portal issues one passcode-protected VHL QR per family member | VHL payload (SHL payload format, flag P) as a CBOR map at HCERT claim -260 key 5 (STT-VHL-001, STT-VHL-002); key generation (STT-VHL-004); JWE dir / A256GCM encryption of each document (STT-VHL-007) | Done: HcertIssuer with Payload.Vhl, HcertVhl.newKey, HcertVhl.encrypt; hosting the manifest and enforcing the passcode are the VHL host’s | . | J4.1 Clinic abroad scans a VHL, fetches with passcode, reads IPS | Verify the VHL HCERT, map or vhlink:/ string at key 5, and the link’s exp (STT-VHL-002, STT-VHL-009); ITI-YY5 request (STT-VHL-005); HTTP Message Signatures (STT-VHL-008); manifest Bundle (STT-VHL-006); decrypt each document (STT-VHL-007) | Done: HcertVerifier.verify, HcertVhl.buildManifestRequest, buildSignatureBase/signatureHeader, parseManifest, decrypt; the HTTP, mutual TLS and AuditEvents are the app’s | .

2160.title: VHL: what the specifications say, and where they disagree
2160.content: Changes raised upstream: WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust#130 (subclaim 5 is a VHL, a CBOR map), WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust-phw#17 (payload types match SMART Health Links), and a patch for IHE ITI.VHL in upstream/ihe-iti-vhl/ (ITI-YY3 key 5 as a CBOR map, example fixes). Open issues OI-21 to OI-29. The IHE ITI VHL profile and the WHO VerifiableHealthLinkPayload model share the SMART Health Links payload fields, but: . | IHE’s manifest is a FHIR List search returning a searchset Bundle of DocumentReferences (ITI-YY5), not the SMART Health Links files[] manifest; the Bundle is not signed, and the journey’s “signed VHL manifests” exist in neither specification. | The value at hcert key 5 is a vhlink:/ text string in ITI-YY3 but a decoded JSON object in the ITI-YY4 example; HCERT 3.2.7.1.5 calls it a SMART Health Link (OI-06). | WHO requires type (vhl) and types exp and v as strings; IHE has no type and uses numbers. | JWE alg/enc are not normative (the example is dir / A256GCM); no zip. | Requester authentication (RFC 9421 HTTP signatures, UDAP, or a VC) and the DID trust list’s mapping to a COSE kid are under-specified. | .

2167.title: A SMART Health Link is the same receipt, with another carrier
2167.content: A plain SMART Health Link (shlink:/, from receiver-scan-credential) is followed by the same steps: the manifest request with the passcode when its P flag is set, the manifest, and each document decrypted. It carries no HCERT, so there is no signature to verify (hcert-verify is skipped) and the receiver cannot tell who issued the link. A “Verifiable SHL” (smart-ips-pilgrimage’s term) is a VHL, verified as above.

2172.title: A SMART Health Link is the same issue, with another carrier
2172.content: A VHL is a SMART Health Link payload carried, signed, in an HCERT (what smart-ips-pilgrimage calls a “Verifiable SHL”). A plain SHL is issued by the same steps (the key, each document encrypted, the manifest, the passcode flag P and exp from the holder’s consent, holder-consent-to-share) with the payload as shlink:/ and base64url JSON instead of HCERT key 5, so it is not signed and the hcert steps are skipped. This skill covers both; the requirements above are the VHL’s.
